item.text:
This pass tested the headline guarantee itself: linearizability under concurrency.

**New tests: propose/read ordering**

- `TestAuditLinearizableReadUnderConcurrency` — 4 workers × 40 propose-then-read iterations on a single-node cluster (160 write/read pairs).
- `TestAuditLinearizableReadAcrossNodes` — 4 workers × 30 iterations on a two-node cluster, with proposals issued on one NodeHost and reads on the other (120 cross-node pairs, so both forwarding paths are exercised).

Both check the documented guarantee — "once a write is completed, all later reads should return the value of that write or a later write" — using a monotonic counter state machine: any read that starts more than 1 ms after a write completed must observe at least that write's value. No stale read in 5/5 runs of each.

**State of the audit**

Three findings, reproduced on the unmodified source and each resolved by a minimal patch in `audit/diag-fixes/` with no regressions:

- F1 — `(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` in [nodehost.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/nodehost.go:2063) misses the engine wakeup (~one RTT latency; one-RTT timeouts fail, two-RTT succeed).
- F2 — `handleCandidateReadIndex` in [raft.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/internal/raft/raft.go:1998) records a dropped ReadIndex twice.
- F3 — `pb.Update.HasUpdate` in [raftpb/raft.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/raftpb/raft.go:112) ignores `DroppedReadIndexes`.

The negative-result catalogue now spans: protocol fuzz (3/5 nodes, loss, reordering, partitions), in-memory log model, vote-survives-restart, colfer entry-encoding property test, follower/observer reads, leader transfer, witness election after leader loss, 1–32 MB payloads (single and two nodes), dropped-read-index idempotence, five-cycle stop/restart endurance with snapshots, and single-node plus cross-node linearizability under concurrency.
